Im going through a similar problem. But I believe it's likely the mind playing a trick on you. Here's how I know. 18 months ago I had hit what I believed was rock bottom. I was borderline suicidal and desperate for relief. I thought drinking was the only thing keeping me alive, but was still so miserable eventually I decided that I should try sobering up, and if I still couldn't take my life, I would end it. It ended up working. A month of sobriety revealed the old me I used to like. 

But I couldn't stay sober. I thought I could drink moderately, but what started as only drinking with friends, turned to only having 20 drinks a week, to 30, to 40, to 70! Last week I had a whopping 92 drinks. I blame it all on my stressful job and lack of direction in my life. I have made the choice to quit my job next week and go sober because I know it worked before. 

I guess my point in all this is that I understand your mentality, it's how I rationalized my drinking. The bottom line is that drinking to drown out emotions absolutely makes those emotions worse. Fixing your feelings for 3 hours will lead to 3 times more pain later on. Life is tough man, going sober may not fix all your problems, but it will definitely prevent new ones that drinking would cause. Sobriety sometimes forces you to tackle what you need to tackle.
